pathway.title: Ziff Davis, Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - Debt service is covered by cash for the next 12 months to 24 months, and after the 1.75% repayment no drawn debt matures before March 2028. Cash was USD 1,407.7 million and the revolving facility offered USD 348.9 million at September 30, 2026, liquidity of USD 1,756.6 million against debt principal of USD 872.3 million, so cash exceeded principal by USD 535.4 million; Financial foundation states no pro forma figure for the repayment of the 1.75% convertible notes after that date, so pro forma cash is not established. The two nearest claims on cash, the USD 149.1 million repayment and USD 130.8 million of income taxes payable, total USD 279.95 million and cash covered them 5.03x. After the repayment, principal of USD 723.2 million remains in the 2028 convertible notes and the 2030 senior notes, both fixed rate and unsecured, with scheduled coupons of USD 30.82 million a year. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 73; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-1; calculation CALC-2; calculation CALC-14; calculation CALC-15; calculation CALC-16; calculation CALC-18

- The cash cushion is being spent quickly, and share repurchases are the largest discretionary use. Cash fell USD 198.4 million in the third quarter of 2026, of which repurchases were USD 92.0 million, 46.36%, and the combined operating outflow USD 77.1 million, 38.85%, so at that rate cash would last 7.09 quarters before the repayment of the 1.75% notes and the tax payment. Nine-month repurchases equal 23.37% of the USD 1,134.1 million of sale proceeds net of cash divested, and finishing the remaining authorization at the September average price would cost USD 327.84 million, 61.23% of the cash above debt principal. No minimum cash balance or leverage target appears in the filings, and the senior notes restrict payments to shareholders only above 3.5x net leverage, a test that on a plain reading does not apply while cash exceeds debt, although the indenture definition is not supplied. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 81; 10-K_2025-12-31_zd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation CALC-4; calculation CALC-5; calculation CALC-6; calculation CALC-8; calculation CALC-9; calculation CALC-10; calculation CALC-11; calculation CALC-12; calculation CALC-21

- Earnings power fell faster than revenue because costs did not flex down. EBITDA before goodwill impairment was USD 146.4 million for nine months against USD 206.2 million, down 29.00%, and its margin fell to 17.35% from 23.59%; in the third quarter it was 14.39% against 25.84%. The cost base, meaning operating costs before depreciation, amortization and goodwill impairment, rose 4.39% while revenue fell 3.48%, and rose 1.94% excluding a USD 16.4 million long-lived asset impairment. Segment operating income before goodwill impairment fell 30.71%, unallocated corporate cost rose 23.89%, and EBITDA of USD 62.0 million is derived from operating income plus depreciation and amortization because the company states none. Adding back the long-lived impairment as well gives USD 162.8 million, down 21.04%, an analyst normalization. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 62; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-24; calculation CALC-26; calculation CALC-27; calculation CALC-28; calculation CALC-29; calculation CALC-30; calculation CALC-33; calculation CALC-34; calculation CALC-37; calculation CALC-38; calculation CALC-39; calculation CALC-40; calculation CALC-43; calculation CALC-44

- Revenue is advertising-led, short-dated and weakening faster than the nine-month figure shows. Advertising and performance marketing was 63.09% of nine-month revenue and fell 6.30%, on agreements that in most cases run one year or less and can be ended without penalty. Revenue fell 5.61% in the third quarter against 2.33% in the first half, and excluding acquired businesses nine-month revenue fell 6.05% against the reported 3.48%. Net advertising retention was below 100% in all three advertising segments and lower than a year earlier: 87.0% against 94.0% in Technology & Shopping, 84.7% against 88.8% in Gaming & Entertainment and 95.9% against 102.1% in Health & Wellness, while Health & Wellness subscription customers fell 22.19%. The company ties the Technology & Shopping decline to traffic pressure, and its risk factors name generative AI as a threat to traffic. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 54–55; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 69; 10-K_2025-12-31_zd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-K_2025-12-31_zd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 34; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-22; calculation CALC-23; calculation CALC-76; calculation CALC-78; calculation CALC-79

- Earnings-based leverage cannot be stated for the continuing business, but its floor is not low. Financial foundation finds it not calculable because the 2025 annual report includes Connectivity; the only bound the filings allow is trailing total-entity EBITDA of USD 239.6 million, which includes Connectivity until June 17, 2026 and so overstates the continuing figure. Debt principal is therefore at least 3.64x that bound, and at least 2.69x before goodwill impairment, while net of cash the group has no net debt. Nine-month EBITDA covered cash interest paid 2.89x unadjusted and 6.82x before goodwill impairment, against 9.09x a year earlier. The credit agreement tests total leverage at 4.00x and interest coverage at 3.00x and the company reports compliance, but the definitions are not supplied, so headroom is not calculable. This adds a bound to Financial foundation and does not replace its conclusion. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-K_2025-12-31_zd-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 128–129; Source readiness (CP-0); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-48; calculation CALC-49; calculation CALC-50; calculation CALC-51; calculation CALC-52; calculation CALC-53; calculation CALC-54; calculation CALC-55; calculation CALC-57; calculation CALC-58; calculation CALC-59

- Impairments show management has cut its own forecasts, and more are possible. Goodwill impairments of USD 84.4 million for nine months, against USD 17.6 million a year earlier, followed forecast reductions in Health & Wellness and Technology & Shopping reporting units, alongside USD 16.4 million of long-lived asset impairments. USD 872.8 million of goodwill, 69.21% of the balance, sits in reporting units with no excess fair value or less than 15% excess, so a further forecast cut can trigger another charge. The charges are non-cash and leave debt service unchanged, but they mark lower expected cash generation and would reduce covenant earnings if the credit agreement does not add them back, which is not supplied. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 56–58; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 62; calculation CALC-65; calculation CALC-66

- Refinancing risk is manageable but concentrated in 2027 and 2028, and the market prices the 2030 senior notes below par. The USD 350.0 million secured revolving facility is undrawn, has USD 348.9 million available, which implies USD 1.1 million of letters of credit, and expires seven months after the as-of date with no extension disclosed. The 2028 convertible notes of USD 263.1 million convert at USD 100 a share against a September average repurchase price of USD 54.93, so repayment in cash at maturity is the likely path. The disclosed fair value of the 2030 senior notes was 91.25% of principal at September 30, 2026 against 94.50% at the 2025 year end, despite the cash build, while the 2028 convertible notes stood at 101.82%; these are fair values disclosed at the period ends from quoted prices or dealer quotes, not current quotations. Noteholders are unsecured and rank behind the secured revolver, which is undrawn; the 2028 convertible notes are also structurally junior to all subsidiary liabilities, while the 2030 senior notes carry guarantees from certain domestic subsidiaries. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 28–31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 33–34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 81; calculation CALC-3; calculation CALC-60; calculation CALC-61; calculation CALC-62; calculation CALC-80

- Financial policy favors shareholders, with no sponsor to support or extract value and no floor on cash for creditors. Repurchases, acquisitions and a debt payment used USD 537.7 million in FY2024, 189.56% of free cash flow of USD 283.68 million, and repurchases and acquisitions used USD 241.1 million in FY2025, 83.76% of USD 287.87 million, both measured with Connectivity included. The share count is down 28.16% since the end of 2023, no dividend was paid in 2023, 2024 or 2025, and the capital allocation strategy lists acquisitions, repurchases and strengthening the balance sheet in that order. Creditors are protected on a change of control by a repurchase offer on the senior notes and an event of default under the credit agreement, and internal control over financial reporting was effective at the 2025 year end. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_zd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_zd-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 83–84; 10-K_2025-12-31_zd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 91; 10-K_2025-12-31_zd-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 129–130; 10-K_2025-12-31_zd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 199; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-81; calculation CALC-82; calculation CALC-83; calculation CALC-84; calculation CALC-85; calculation CALC-86; calculation CALC-87

- Claims outside the debt figure are modest, but a float is unwinding and a tax bill has no stated date. Settlement payables to gift-card customers fell USD 269.5 million to USD 199.6 million while settlement receivables fell USD 159.4 million, so payables net of receivables fell from USD 155.7 million to USD 45.6 million, and the gift-card business reduced nine-month operating cash flow by USD 98.5 million; the filings do not say how much cash is held against these payables. Income taxes payable of USD 130.8 million relate to the sale gain and carry no payment date. Future operating lease payments are USD 31.0 million, of which USD 6.9 million fall within twelve months, and indirect tax reserves are USD 17.3 million; no finance leases, factoring, supplier finance, defined benefit pension or retiree medical obligations are disclosed. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 73; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 75; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-67; calculation CALC-68; calculation CALC-69; calculation CALC-70; calculation CALC-88; calculation CALC-89

cells.text: Vertically focused digital media and internet company with four reportable segments: Technology & Shopping, Gaming & Entertainment, Health & Wellness and Cybersecurity & Martech; the fifth segment, Connectivity, was sold on 2026-06-17
Three segments are advertising-led and one is subscription-led, so cash flow follows advertiser budgets and web traffic
Revenue of USD 843.705 million for nine months 2026: advertising and performance marketing 63.09%, subscription and licensing 34.97%, other 1.94%
Down 3.48% on the prior year; down 6.05% excluding acquired businesses
Most advertiser agreements run one year or less and can be terminated at any time by the advertiser or the company without penalty
Little contracted revenue protects the advertising line in a downturn

Visitors come through search engine marketing and optimization, email and social media referrals; the company cites traffic pressure on affiliate commerce and display advertising in Technology & Shopping
Search algorithm and platform changes can cut revenue faster than costs can be cut
Of revenue for nine months 2026: sales and marketing 43.1%, general and administrative 18.8%, depreciation and amortization 16.3%, direct costs 15.8%, research and engineering 4.9%
Marketing and overhead are the largest costs and rose as a share of revenue as revenue fell

Operating loss of USD 75.401 million, or operating income of USD 8.988 million before goodwill impairment of USD 84.389 million; segment operating income: Gaming & Entertainment USD 27.958 million, Cybersecurity & Martech USD 31.156 million, Technology & Shopping loss of USD 48.562 million, Health & Wellness loss of USD 16.355 million
Two of four segments lose money after impairments; corporate costs rose 23.89%
Digital media revenue is generally higher in the fourth quarter holiday period; Cybersecurity & Martech usage and sign-ups are lower than average in the fourth quarter
Nine-month shares understate the fourth-quarter advertising weight

Quarterly average customers fell in all three subscription segments: Gaming & Entertainment 483,000 against 514,000, Health & Wellness 1,480,000 against 1,902,000, Cybersecurity & Martech 1,223,000 against 1,232,000
Revenue per customer rose in two of three segments, so nine-month subscription revenue was down only 0.38% while the customer base shrank

runs.text: The first strength is liquidity. Cash of USD 1,407.7 million exceeded debt principal by USD 535.4 million and the undrawn revolving facility added USD 348.9 million, so near-term debt service does not depend on earnings; pro forma cash after the later repayment of the 1.75% convertible notes is not established. The mechanism is that cash held in treasury funds and demand deposits can be applied to any maturity without a refinancing, which keeps the probability of default low over the next 12 months to 24 months. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 77; calculation CALC-1; calculation CALC-2

The second strength is a plain debt structure. The remaining principal of USD 723.2 million is fixed rate and unsecured, with 36.39% due in 2028 and 63.61% in 2030, scheduled coupons of USD 30.82 million a year, no hedging contracts and no drawn secured debt, so a rate rise cannot reset the cost of the existing notes. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 77–78; calculation CALC-16; calculation CALC-18; calculation CALC-71; calculation CALC-72

The third strength is the absence of a sponsor and of a dividend. No controlling shareholder is stated, no dividend was paid in 2023, 2024 or 2025, and the notes carry change-of-control repurchase rights, so there is no owner with an incentive to extract cash through the capital structure and creditors can exit on a takeover. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_zd-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 83–84; 10-K_2025-12-31_zd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 91; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The fourth strength is the equity value beneath the debt. At the September average repurchase price of USD 54.93 the 33.1 million shares outstanding were worth about USD 1,818.3 million, 2.08x debt principal, an analyst illustration that depends on the share price holding. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 81; calculation CALC-63; calculation CALC-64

The first weakness is shrinking, cancellable advertising revenue. Advertising was 63.09% of nine-month revenue and fell 6.30% on agreements that most often run one year or less, and retention fell below 100% in all three advertising segments, so advertisers can cut spend faster than costs can follow, which lowers the earnings that support the 2028 and 2030 notes. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 54–55; 10-K_2025-12-31_zd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 29; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The second weakness is margin loss. EBITDA before goodwill impairment fell 29.00% for nine months and its margin to 17.35% from 23.59%, because the cost base, meaning operating costs before depreciation, amortization and goodwill impairment, rose 4.39% while revenue fell 3.48%, so operating leverage is working against creditors. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation CALC-26; calculation CALC-27; calculation CALC-28; calculation CALC-29; calculation CALC-30; calculation CALC-37

The third weakness is the use of cash. Repurchases of USD 265.0 million came while combined free cash flow was an outflow of USD 49.3 million, and at the third-quarter rate cash would last 7.09 quarters, so the cushion that protects creditors is being converted into shareholder returns without a stated floor. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation CALC-10; calculation CALC-19

The fourth weakness is goodwill at risk. USD 872.8 million of goodwill, 69.21% of the balance, sits in reporting units with no excess fair value or less than 15% excess, so another forecast cut would add a non-cash charge and could lower covenant earnings if impairments are not added back. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 57; calculation CALC-65; calculation CALC-66

The fifth weakness is the thin backstop and the open leverage definition. The revolving facility expires seven months after the as-of date with no extension disclosed, the covenant definitions are not supplied, and debt principal is at least 3.64x the only earnings bound the filings allow, so a weaker 2027 could meet a refinancing and a covenant test together. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 33–34; calculation CALC-54

cells.text: Ziff Davis, Inc., a Delaware corporation with headquarters in New York; common stock listed on the Nasdaq Stock Market as ZD; large accelerated filer

No controlling shareholder or sponsor is stated; 138 registered holders at 2026-02-18 against 146 at 2025-02-21, excluding street-name holders; holders above 10% are excluded from the non-affiliate value without being named
33,102,280 shares outstanding at 2026-09-30, from 38,376,859 at 2025-12-31 and 46,078,464 at 2023-12-31, a fall of 28.16% since 2023; no dividends paid in 2023, 2024 or 2025

The Board approves share repurchases; its Audit Committee approves related-party transactions and oversees cyber risk; KPMG LLP audits; internal control over financial reporting was effective at 2025-12-31; directors and independence are not supplied
Revenue for nine months 2026: Health & Wellness 32.38%, Technology & Shopping 27.25%, Cybersecurity & Martech 24.50%, Gaming & Entertainment 15.88%
The United States was 84.01% of FY2025 revenue, with the rest from other countries; the share includes Connectivity
About 3,900 employees at 2025-12-31, 55% in the United States, including Connectivity; about 110 editorial employees voluntarily recognized a union

About USD 3.3 billion deployed on close to a hundred acquisitions since 2012, mostly tuck-ins by count; consideration was USD 365.1 million in 2024, USD 81.9 million in 2025 and USD 8.4 million in nine months 2026

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: On 2026-03-02 Ziff Davis agreed to sell its Connectivity business, the Ookla group of broadband testing and insight brands, to Accenture Inc. for an aggregate cash price of USD 1,200 million, subject to customary adjustments, and completed the sale on 2026-06-17. Total proceeds were USD 1,216.1 million, being USD 1,179.1 million at closing plus USD 37.0 million in escrow, and cash received at closing net of USD 45.0 million of cash divested was USD 1,134.1 million. The escrow holds USD 12.0 million for working-capital adjustments, to be settled within 120 days of closing and still a receivable at September 30, 2026, and USD 25.0 million for indemnifications, payable on the earlier of settlement of indemnification matters or three years after closing. Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_zd-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-06-30_zd-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-06-30_zd-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20

Ziff Davis recorded a pre-tax gain on sale of USD 860.6 million within discontinued operations and elected not to allocate interest expense to the discontinued business. It plans to use the proceeds for general corporate purposes and capital allocation activities, subject to the conditions of its outstanding debt securities, and has not itemized any use beyond share repurchases and the tax on the gain. A transition services agreement has Ziff Davis provide accounting, tax, treasury, technology and human resource services to Accenture for up to twelve months from closing, extendable by two three-month periods, at Connectivity's expense; USD 4.8 million was due from Accenture at quarter-end, and Ziff Davis states it has no other significant involvement with Connectivity. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 20–22

No new debt was issued in nine months 2026: the cash flow statement shows no borrowing or debt payment, no 4.625% senior notes were repurchased in the period and the revolving credit facility had no balance. The debt stack comes from earlier steps: USD 550.0 million of 1.75% convertible notes issued on 2019-11-15; USD 750.0 million of 4.625% senior notes due 2030 issued on 2020-10-07, of which about USD 289.96 million has since been repurchased, leaving USD 460.04 million; a revolving credit agreement signed on 2021-04-07 and raised to USD 350.0 million on 2024-06-18, with maturity moved to 2027-06-18; and the exchange of 2024-07-16, in which USD 400.9 million of the 1.75% notes was swapped, with certain holders, for USD 263.1 million of 3.625% convertible notes due 2028 plus USD 135.0 million in cash. The remaining USD 149.1 million of 1.75% notes was repaid in cash after September 30, 2026, leaving principal of USD 723.2 million in the 2028 and 2030 notes. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 28–30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 48; calculation C94; calculation C95; calculation C71; calculation C96; calculation C48; calculation C47

Shareholder returns are the other recurring transaction. The repurchase program, first approved on 2020-08-06, was enlarged on 2024-08-02 and again on 2026-02-22, when its expiry moved to 2036-02-22; cumulative repurchases since 2020 cost USD 1,015.8 million, and completing the remaining authorization at September's average price would cost USD 327.84 million. Acquisitions were small: two immaterial purchases for USD 8.4 million in nine months 2026, after USD 81.9 million in 2025 and USD 365.1 million in 2024, which included TDS Gift Cards and CNET Media. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 76; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 81; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_zd-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 151–152

fields.value: This source-readiness review covers Ziff Davis, Inc. (issuer zd-1084048), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is five periodic SEC filings, two annual reports and three 2026 quarterly reports, assessed for Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit work. It draws no credit conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The five supplied filings give creditors a primary-source base for financial, business and fundamental credit work on Ziff Davis, Inc., but they cannot test covenant headroom, ratings or legal priority, so those questions stay open until further documents arrive. Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit can proceed on these filings alone, each with the limitations below.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main limit is a break in perimeter. The Connectivity business was sold on June 17, 2026; the three 2026 quarterly reports present its results as discontinued and restate the December 31, 2025 balance sheet, while the 2025 annual report still includes it and the 2026 cash flow statements mix continuing and discontinued operations. Full-year 2025 figures on the continuing basis are therefore not printed. No executed indenture or credit agreement, credit rating or company-defined adjusted earnings measure is supplied, board and ownership detail sits in a proxy statement that is not supplied, and the 1.75% convertible notes were repaid after September 30, 2026 on a date the filing does not state.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial foundation for Ziff Davis, Inc. (issuer zd-1084048), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is five periodic SEC filings covering FY2024, FY2025 and the first three quarters of 2026, from which it builds statement tables, debt, liquidity and ratio figures with their limits. It makes no credit recommendation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ziff Davis held more cash than debt at the end of the third quarter of 2026 after selling Connectivity, which cushions creditors near term, but earnings-based leverage on the continuing business cannot be calculated from the filings. Cash was USD 1,407.7 million against carrying-value debt of USD 868.2 million, a net cash position of USD 539.5 million, and the revolving credit facility was undrawn with USD 348.9 million available. At the 2025 year end, before the sale, net debt was USD 259.5 million, or 0.63x EBITDA of USD 411.8 million, derived from operating income and depreciation and including Connectivity.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The cushion is not recurring cash generation: free cash flow for nine months 2026 was an outflow of USD 49.3 million on a combined basis, and income taxes payable of USD 130.8 million were owed at quarter-end. The 1.75% convertible notes of USD 149.1 million were repaid after quarter-end, leaving notes of USD 723.2 million due in 2028 and 2030.

Proceeds net of cash divested were USD 1,134.1 million.

The revolver commitment of USD 350.0 million is secured, undrawn and matures seven months after the as-of date with no extension disclosed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against comfort is on earnings, not on the balance sheet: the continuing business reported an operating loss of USD 75.4 million for nine months 2026, net advertising revenue retention fell in all three advertising segments between the third quarters of 2025 and 2026, and subscription customer counts fell in all three subscription segments. The net cash position is a one-time result of the sale, so a durable view needs last-twelve-months EBITDA on the continuing basis, which no filing prints yet. The view would improve if recast full-year 2025 figures show EBITDA that comfortably covers the remaining notes and interest, and would weaken if buybacks, acquisitions or the tax payment on the sale gain used up the cash balance, which stood at USD 1,407.7 million at quarter-end before the 1.75% repayment.

fields.value: The issuer states no adjusted EBITDA, so the bridge has no stated steps.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Full-year 2025 and last-twelve-months figures on the continuing basis are not printed, so Total debt / EBITDA, Net debt / EBITDA and EBITDA / cash interest at September 30, 2026 are not calculable, and the fourth quarter of 2025 on the continuing basis is not stated in the revenue and EBITDA chart. The 2025 annual report includes Connectivity while the 2026 reports exclude it, so the last-twelve-months construction is not comparable (High). Closing it needs recast full-year 2025 continuing results from a later filing or a lender presentation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The 2026 cash flow statements combine continuing and discontinued operations and do not print the operating cash flow of Connectivity, so continuing operating cash flow and free cash flow for nine months 2026 are not directly sourced and are shown on the combined basis (High). The operating cash flow of the discontinued business from a later filing would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The issuer states no EBITDA or adjusted EBITDA in any period, so EBITDA (Reported) is derived as operating income plus depreciation and amortization, includes goodwill impairments and has no adjusted twin; the EBITDA bridge is therefore not stated (Medium). A company reconciliation or the covenant definition would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The covenant levels of the Credit Agreement are printed but the reported leverage and coverage ratios and the EBITDA definitions behind them are not, so covenant headroom is not calculable (High for covenant work). The executed credit agreement and a compliance certificate would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The 1.75% convertible notes were repaid after September 30, 2026, but the filing gives no repayment date, no interest paid and no pro forma balances, so every figure of the post-balance-sheet table is not supplied (Medium). A current report or the next quarterly report would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The revolver matures on the earlier of June 18, 2027 or an earlier date under limited circumstances that did not occur, seven months after the as-of date, and no extension is disclosed; availability of USD 348.9 million is net of letters of credit whose amount is not printed separately (Medium). A later filing stating an extension or replacement and the letters-of-credit amount would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Income taxes payable of USD 130.8 million at quarter-end, up because of the tax on the sale gain, have no printed payment date, so their effect on cash after the balance-sheet date is not established (Medium). The next quarterly report would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 72; calculation C68

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash of USD 158.6 million is held in foreign jurisdictions; the 2025 annual report says foreign earnings are treated as permanently reinvested or remittable substantially free of additional taxes and that the tax cost of repatriating them is not practicable to determine, so the access cost of this cash is not established (Low). The liquidity analysis should treat it as cash with an unstated access cost.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The balance sheet at September 30, 2025 is not in the sources, so the nine-month 2025 columns have no balance-sheet pair and net debt for that date is not supplied (Low). The September 2025 quarterly report would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The notes are described as guaranteed on an unsecured basis by certain domestic wholly-owned subsidiaries and the revolver as secured by the guarantors' assets, but no guarantor is named and the two convertible issues state no subsidiary guarantee, so the debt stack states obligors only as printed (Medium for structural analysis). The executed documents and the list of subsidiaries would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Statement lines the issuer prints only in some periods are written as not supplied in the other columns: the loss on sale of businesses, gains and credit-loss provisions on investments and the net income split on the income statement, the held-for-sale balance-sheet lines, and the debt payment line of the cash flow statement; a printed dash is also written as not supplied and never as zero (Low). No action is needed beyond reading the filing's own presentation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The cash flow table reproduces the totals and the lines that matter for credit, being net income, depreciation, share-based compensation, impairment, the gain or loss on sale, deferred tax, capital expenditure, acquisitions, disposals, debt payment and repurchases; the remaining non-cash adjustments and working-capital lines are in the filings and are summed as a calculated working-capital change instead of being reproduced one by one (Low). The filings themselves hold the lines.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The revolver's drawn spread and any floor are not stated because nothing is drawn, only the margin ranges are printed, and the revolver's scheduled amortisation is not stated (Low). The executed credit agreement would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Claims outside the debt figure are not in Total Debt and are not netted in net debt: future minimum operating lease payments of USD 31.0 million at quarter-end, indirect tax reserves of USD 17.3 million, a liability for uncertain tax positions of USD 19.1 million, settlement payables, revenue-sharing minimum guarantees and cloud and similar commitments whose amounts are not printed, and litigation for which no material loss is accrued; the filings disclose no finance leases, factoring, supplier finance, securitization, defined benefit pension or retiree medical obligations, and the only retirement plan described is a defined contribution 401(k) plan (Low). The amounts that are not printed would close the gap.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business and governance fact pack for Ziff Davis, Inc. (issuer zd-1084048), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the five supplied periodic filings covering FY2024, FY2025 and the first three quarters of 2026, used for the business, the Connectivity sale, ownership and control, governance, capital allocation and disclosure. It makes no credit recommendation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ziff Davis is a publicly listed, advertising-led media company with no controlling shareholder or sponsor stated, so creditors rely on its own cash and earnings rather than owner support, and governance risk rests on how freely it returns cash to shareholders. At September 30, 2026 cash of USD 1,407.7 million exceeded debt principal of USD 872.3 million after the sale of Connectivity for USD 1,200 million, but continuing operations lost USD 75.4 million at the operating line over nine months and USD 265.0 million of cash went to share repurchases.

fields.value: - The remaining business is advertising-led, shrinking and weakening at the profit line. Advertising and performance marketing revenue was USD 532.3 million for nine months 2026, 63.09% of revenue and down 6.30% on the prior year, on advertiser agreements that in most cases run one year or less and can be ended without penalty. The company attributes the Technology & Shopping decline to traffic pressure on affiliate commerce and display advertising, and net advertising retention fell in all three advertising segments between the third quarters of 2025 and 2026. Revenue excluding acquired businesses fell 6.05%, against a reported fall of 3.48%.

fields.value: - Earnings quality has deteriorated, and the impairments show that management lowered its own forecasts for several units. Operating results swung from income of USD 39.7 million to a loss of USD 75.4 million, including goodwill impairments of USD 84.4 million that followed reductions in forecast revenue and earnings in the Health & Wellness and Technology & Shopping units. Excluding goodwill impairment, operating income was USD 8.99 million against USD 57.23 million. Goodwill of USD 872.8 million, 69.21% of the balance, sits in units with no or thin valuation headroom, so further non-cash charges would follow if forecasts slip again. Technology & Shopping and Health & Wellness lost money at segment level for nine months while Cybersecurity & Martech improved.

fields.value: - The sale turned a subscription business with stable margins into cash, and the cash is now open to use by management. The USD 1,200 million price was 15.77x FY2025 segment operating income of USD 76.1 million and 11.41x that figure plus depreciation and amortization, and total proceeds were USD 1,216.1 million including USD 37.0 million held in escrow. Income taxes payable rose by USD 123.5 million to USD 130.8 million, tied by the company to the gain on the sale, with no payment date stated. The business that remains leans more on advertising: advertising was 56.75% of FY2025 revenue with Connectivity and 63.09% for nine months 2026 without it.

fields.value: - Capital allocation is shareholder-oriented and has at times exceeded free cash flow. In FY2024 repurchases, acquisitions and a debt payment used USD 537.7 million, 189.56% of free cash flow of USD 283.68 million; in FY2025 repurchases and acquisitions used USD 241.1 million, 83.76% of free cash flow of USD 287.87 million, both measured with Connectivity included. In nine months 2026 repurchases were USD 265.0 million, 23.37% of the net sale proceeds, while free cash flow on the combined basis was an outflow of USD 49.3 million. The share count is down 28.16% since the end of 2023, no dividend has been paid, and the authorization was enlarged in February 2026 to run to 2036; finishing it at September's average price would cost USD 327.84 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No sponsor or controlling holder is stated, so creditors have no owner to lean on and, as far as the filings show, no owner extraction to guard against, and they are protected if control changes. The filings state no controlling shareholder and no sponsor, and the proxy statement that would name the larger holders and directors is not supplied. The senior notes require an offer to repurchase on a change of control, the revolving credit agreement lists a change of control as an event of default, and Delaware takeover law and board-issuable preferred stock make a hostile approach harder.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The debt terms leave room for shareholder returns while leverage is low, and that room is not verified. The senior notes limit restricted payments only when net leverage is above 3.5x, and above that level allow the greater of USD 250 million and 50.0% of EBITDA; the revolving credit agreement restricts distributions subject to customary exceptions and tests total leverage at 4.00x and interest coverage at 3.00x, with compliance stated at September 30, 2026. Basket sizes, the covenant earnings definition and the guarantor list sit in executed documents that are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Governance disclosure is adequate on controls and audit but thin on the board and ownership. Internal control over financial reporting was effective at December 31, 2025 with an unqualified auditor opinion, and disclosure controls were effective at September 30, 2026, but a material weakness identified in the past was remediated on a date the filings do not give. The one related-party exposure is an investment fund with a carrying value and maximum exposure of USD 99.9 million, 4.69% of stockholders' equity, approved by the Audit Committee, with no further capital required. Directors, independence, executive pay and holders above stated thresholds are incorporated from a proxy statement that is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Acquisition activity has slowed sharply, which lowers integration and funding risk, but the stated policy still treats acquisitions as a core use of capital. Total consideration was USD 365.1 million in 2024, USD 81.9 million in 2025 and USD 8.4 million in nine months 2026, against about USD 3.3 billion deployed since 2012. The annual and quarterly reports describe 2025 differently, seven purchases for USD 81.9 million against six for USD 81.3 million, a difference the filings do not explain.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against caution is the balance sheet and the absence of an owner with an extraction incentive. Cash exceeded debt principal by USD 535.39 million, the USD 350.0 million revolving facility was undrawn with USD 348.9 million available, no dividend was paid in 2023, 2024 or 2025, free cash flow was USD 287.87 million in FY2025 with Connectivity included, controls over financial reporting were effective with an unqualified audit opinion, and the related-party note discloses one fund investment that needs no further capital. The view would improve if management committed the sale proceeds to debt reduction or a stated minimum cash balance, or if recast continuing results showed stable advertising revenue and positive free cash flow. It would weaken if repurchases continue at the nine-month pace, because finishing the remaining authorization at September's average price would use USD 327.84 million, 61.23% of the cash above debt principal, while taxes of USD 130.8 million are payable and the revolving facility matures on 2027-06-18, or if acquisitions return to the 2024 scale funded from sale cash.

fields.value: - The proxy statement is not supplied, so the conclusion that no controlling shareholder or sponsor is stated cannot be confirmed; a holder above the stated thresholds, a nomination agreement or an activist position would change the reading of capital-return and sale decisions.

fields.value: - FY2025 revenue and segment profit include Connectivity and no full-year continuing figures are printed, so the finding on the shift toward advertising rests on nine-month comparisons; the seasonally stronger fourth quarter could change the advertising share.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No management presentation, earnings release or guidance figure is supplied, so the finding that forecasts were lowered rests on impairment disclosures alone; management's own outlook could soften or sharpen it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The latest document is dated 2026-11-06, so the date and interest of the 1.75% notes repayment and the settlement of the USD 12.0 million working-capital escrow are not established; either could change the size of the cash cushion over debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On 2026-03-02 Ziff Davis agreed to sell its Connectivity business, the Ookla group of broadband testing and insight brands, to Accenture Inc. for an aggregate cash price of USD 1,200 million, subject to customary adjustments, and completed the sale on 2026-06-17. Total proceeds were USD 1,216.1 million, being USD 1,179.1 million at closing plus USD 37.0 million in escrow, and cash received at closing net of USD 45.0 million of cash divested was USD 1,134.1 million. The escrow holds USD 12.0 million for working-capital adjustments, to be settled within 120 days of closing and still a receivable at September 30, 2026, and USD 25.0 million for indemnifications, payable on the earlier of settlement of indemnification matters or three years after closing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ziff Davis recorded a pre-tax gain on sale of USD 860.6 million within discontinued operations and elected not to allocate interest expense to the discontinued business. It plans to use the proceeds for general corporate purposes and capital allocation activities, subject to the conditions of its outstanding debt securities, and has not itemized any use beyond share repurchases and the tax on the gain. A transition services agreement has Ziff Davis provide accounting, tax, treasury, technology and human resource services to Accenture for up to twelve months from closing, extendable by two three-month periods, at Connectivity's expense; USD 4.8 million was due from Accenture at quarter-end, and Ziff Davis states it has no other significant involvement with Connectivity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No new debt was issued in nine months 2026: the cash flow statement shows no borrowing or debt payment, no 4.625% senior notes were repurchased in the period and the revolving credit facility had no balance. The debt stack comes from earlier steps: USD 550.0 million of 1.75% convertible notes issued on 2019-11-15; USD 750.0 million of 4.625% senior notes due 2030 issued on 2020-10-07, of which about USD 289.96 million has since been repurchased, leaving USD 460.04 million; a revolving credit agreement signed on 2021-04-07 and raised to USD 350.0 million on 2024-06-18, with maturity moved to 2027-06-18; and the exchange of 2024-07-16, in which USD 400.9 million of the 1.75% notes was swapped, with certain holders, for USD 263.1 million of 3.625% convertible notes due 2028 plus USD 135.0 million in cash. The remaining USD 149.1 million of 1.75% notes was repaid in cash after September 30, 2026, leaving principal of USD 723.2 million in the 2028 and 2030 notes.

The repurchase program, first approved on 2020-08-06, was enlarged on 2024-08-02 and again on 2026-02-22, when its expiry moved to 2036-02-22; cumulative repurchases since 2020 cost USD 1,015.8 million, and completing the remaining authorization at September's average price would cost USD 327.84 million. Acquisitions were small: two immaterial purchases for USD 8.4 million in nine months 2026, after USD 81.9 million in 2025 and USD 365.1 million in 2024, which included TDS Gift Cards and CNET Media.

fields.value: Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. The level is driven by cash returned to shareholders from sale proceeds, because it can shrink the cash cushion over debt, which implies weaker cover for the 2027 revolver maturity and the 2028 and 2030 notes; countervailing evidence is cash above debt principal, no dividends and no sponsor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: This synthesis covers Ziff Davis, Inc. (issuer zd-1084048), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the fundamental credit profile of the business after the sale of Connectivity, built from five periodic SEC filings and the supplied source readiness, financial foundation and business and governance analyses. It assigns no rating and makes no security recommendation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ziff Davis can meet its debt service from cash for the next 12 months to 24 months, but the cash came from selling Connectivity rather than from earnings, so noteholders depend on management not spending it. Cash was USD 1,407.7 million against debt principal of USD 872.3 million at September 30, 2026, and pro forma cash after the 1.75% convertible notes were repaid after that date is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings fell sharply: nine-month EBITDA was USD 62.0 million against USD 188.6 million a year earlier, and USD 146.4 million against USD 206.2 million before goodwill impairment, while combined free cash flow was an outflow of USD 49.3 million and USD 265.0 million went to share repurchases. The view weakens if repurchases continue at the third-quarter pace.

fields.value: - Debt service is covered by cash for the next 12 months to 24 months, and after the 1.75% repayment no drawn debt matures before March 2028. Cash was USD 1,407.7 million and the revolving facility offered USD 348.9 million at September 30, 2026, liquidity of USD 1,756.6 million against debt principal of USD 872.3 million, so cash exceeded principal by USD 535.4 million; Financial foundation states no pro forma figure for the repayment of the 1.75% convertible notes after that date, so pro forma cash is not established. The two nearest claims on cash, the USD 149.1 million repayment and USD 130.8 million of income taxes payable, total USD 279.95 million and cash covered them 5.03x. After the repayment, principal of USD 723.2 million remains in the 2028 convertible notes and the 2030 senior notes, both fixed rate and unsecured, with scheduled coupons of USD 30.82 million a year.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The cash cushion is being spent quickly, and share repurchases are the largest discretionary use. Cash fell USD 198.4 million in the third quarter of 2026, of which repurchases were USD 92.0 million, 46.36%, and the combined operating outflow USD 77.1 million, 38.85%, so at that rate cash would last 7.09 quarters before the repayment of the 1.75% notes and the tax payment. Nine-month repurchases equal 23.37% of the USD 1,134.1 million of sale proceeds net of cash divested, and finishing the remaining authorization at the September average price would cost USD 327.84 million, 61.23% of the cash above debt principal. No minimum cash balance or leverage target appears in the filings, and the senior notes restrict payments to shareholders only above 3.5x net leverage, a test that on a plain reading does not apply while cash exceeds debt, although the indenture definition is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Earnings power fell faster than revenue because costs did not flex down. EBITDA before goodwill impairment was USD 146.4 million for nine months against USD 206.2 million, down 29.00%, and its margin fell to 17.35% from 23.59%; in the third quarter it was 14.39% against 25.84%. The cost base, meaning operating costs before depreciation, amortization and goodwill impairment, rose 4.39% while revenue fell 3.48%, and rose 1.94% excluding a USD 16.4 million long-lived asset impairment. Segment operating income before goodwill impairment fell 30.71%, unallocated corporate cost rose 23.89%, and EBITDA of USD 62.0 million is derived from operating income plus depreciation and amortization because the company states none. Adding back the long-lived impairment as well gives USD 162.8 million, down 21.04%, an analyst normalization.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Revenue is advertising-led, short-dated and weakening faster than the nine-month figure shows. Advertising and performance marketing was 63.09% of nine-month revenue and fell 6.30%, on agreements that in most cases run one year or less and can be ended without penalty. Revenue fell 5.61% in the third quarter against 2.33% in the first half, and excluding acquired businesses nine-month revenue fell 6.05% against the reported 3.48%. Net advertising retention was below 100% in all three advertising segments and lower than a year earlier: 87.0% against 94.0% in Technology & Shopping, 84.7% against 88.8% in Gaming & Entertainment and 95.9% against 102.1% in Health & Wellness, while Health & Wellness subscription customers fell 22.19%. The company ties the Technology & Shopping decline to traffic pressure, and its risk factors name generative AI as a threat to traffic.

fields.value: - Earnings-based leverage cannot be stated for the continuing business, but its floor is not low. Financial foundation finds it not calculable because the 2025 annual report includes Connectivity; the only bound the filings allow is trailing total-entity EBITDA of USD 239.6 million, which includes Connectivity until June 17, 2026 and so overstates the continuing figure. Debt principal is therefore at least 3.64x that bound, and at least 2.69x before goodwill impairment, while net of cash the group has no net debt. Nine-month EBITDA covered cash interest paid 2.89x unadjusted and 6.82x before goodwill impairment, against 9.09x a year earlier. The credit agreement tests total leverage at 4.00x and interest coverage at 3.00x and the company reports compliance, but the definitions are not supplied, so headroom is not calculable. This adds a bound to Financial foundation and does not replace its conclusion.

fields.value: - Impairments show management has cut its own forecasts, and more are possible. Goodwill impairments of USD 84.4 million for nine months, against USD 17.6 million a year earlier, followed forecast reductions in Health & Wellness and Technology & Shopping reporting units, alongside USD 16.4 million of long-lived asset impairments. USD 872.8 million of goodwill, 69.21% of the balance, sits in reporting units with no excess fair value or less than 15% excess, so a further forecast cut can trigger another charge. The charges are non-cash and leave debt service unchanged, but they mark lower expected cash generation and would reduce covenant earnings if the credit agreement does not add them back, which is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Refinancing risk is manageable but concentrated in 2027 and 2028, and the market prices the 2030 senior notes below par. The USD 350.0 million secured revolving facility is undrawn, has USD 348.9 million available, which implies USD 1.1 million of letters of credit, and expires seven months after the as-of date with no extension disclosed. The 2028 convertible notes of USD 263.1 million convert at USD 100 a share against a September average repurchase price of USD 54.93, so repayment in cash at maturity is the likely path. The disclosed fair value of the 2030 senior notes was 91.25% of principal at September 30, 2026 against 94.50% at the 2025 year end, despite the cash build, while the 2028 convertible notes stood at 101.82%; these are fair values disclosed at the period ends from quoted prices or dealer quotes, not current quotations. Noteholders are unsecured and rank behind the secured revolver, which is undrawn; the 2028 convertible notes are also structurally junior to all subsidiary liabilities, while the 2030 senior notes carry guarantees from certain domestic subsidiaries.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Financial policy favors shareholders, with no sponsor to support or extract value and no floor on cash for creditors. Repurchases, acquisitions and a debt payment used USD 537.7 million in FY2024, 189.56% of free cash flow of USD 283.68 million, and repurchases and acquisitions used USD 241.1 million in FY2025, 83.76% of USD 287.87 million, both measured with Connectivity included. The share count is down 28.16% since the end of 2023, no dividend was paid in 2023, 2024 or 2025, and the capital allocation strategy lists acquisitions, repurchases and strengthening the balance sheet in that order. Creditors are protected on a change of control by a repurchase offer on the senior notes and an event of default under the credit agreement, and internal control over financial reporting was effective at the 2025 year end.

fields.value: - Claims outside the debt figure are modest, but a float is unwinding and a tax bill has no stated date. Settlement payables to gift-card customers fell USD 269.5 million to USD 199.6 million while settlement receivables fell USD 159.4 million, so payables net of receivables fell from USD 155.7 million to USD 45.6 million, and the gift-card business reduced nine-month operating cash flow by USD 98.5 million; the filings do not say how much cash is held against these payables. Income taxes payable of USD 130.8 million relate to the sale gain and carry no payment date. Future operating lease payments are USD 31.0 million, of which USD 6.9 million fall within twelve months, and indirect tax reserves are USD 17.3 million; no finance leases, factoring, supplier finance, defined benefit pension or retiree medical obligations are disclosed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against caution is the balance sheet and the calendar. Cash exceeded debt principal by USD 535.4 million, the revolving facility was undrawn, after the 1.75% repayment nothing drawn matures before March 2028, net interest turned to income in the third quarter, and at the September average repurchase price the equity was worth about USD 1,818.3 million, 2.08x debt principal, an analyst illustration and not a market quotation. The fourth quarter is the seasonal peak: it earned 34.97% of FY2025 total-entity EBITDA, so the trailing earnings the filings cannot yet show may recover, and the company states that cash, operating cash flow and revolver availability are sufficient for at least the next 12 months.

It would weaken if repurchases stay near USD 92.0 million a quarter while operating cash flow stays negative, if the revolving facility is not extended before its June 2027 expiry, if a further goodwill charge lands in the reporting units with no excess fair value, or if the 2030 senior notes fall further below the 91.25% of principal disclosed at quarter end.
