fields.value: - The conclusion that cash covers debt service for the next 12 months to 24 months rests on cash alone, because no continuing-basis cash flow is printed for 2026; a lower true operating burn than the combined figures show would lengthen the runway and a higher one would shorten it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The floor on gross leverage uses total-entity earnings that include Connectivity until the sale, so it can only say leverage is at least that high; if Connectivity earned more than the filings imply, continuing leverage is higher than the floor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The view that covenants are not a near-term constraint rests on the company's compliance statement, because covenant earnings, the treatment of impairments and whether leverage is measured gross or net of cash are not supplied; those definitions decide whether the printed levels are remote or close.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The market reading of the 2030 senior notes uses fair values disclosed at the period ends and no current quotations, so the signal that the market is less comfortable than the balance sheet is indicative and could differ at today's prices.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The date, interest and effect of the 1.75% repayment and the timing of the tax payment are not stated, so the cash runway and the cash cover of near claims are measured at September 30, 2026 and would be lower after those payments.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No management guidance is supplied, so the 12-month to 24-month outlook is the analyst's reading of three quarters of trend, and a recovery in the seasonally strong fourth quarter would soften the earnings conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first strength is liquidity. Cash of USD 1,407.7 million exceeded debt principal by USD 535.4 million and the undrawn revolving facility added USD 348.9 million, so near-term debt service does not depend on earnings; pro forma cash after the later repayment of the 1.75% convertible notes is not established. The mechanism is that cash held in treasury funds and demand deposits can be applied to any maturity without a refinancing, which keeps the probability of default low over the next 12 months to 24 months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 77; calculation CALC-1; calculation CALC-2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second strength is a plain debt structure. The remaining principal of USD 723.2 million is fixed rate and unsecured, with 36.39% due in 2028 and 63.61% in 2030, scheduled coupons of USD 30.82 million a year, no hedging contracts and no drawn secured debt, so a rate rise cannot reset the cost of the existing notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 77–78; calculation CALC-16; calculation CALC-18; calculation CALC-71; calculation CALC-72

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third strength is the absence of a sponsor and of a dividend. No controlling shareholder is stated, no dividend was paid in 2023, 2024 or 2025, and the notes carry change-of-control repurchase rights, so there is no owner with an incentive to extract cash through the capital structure and creditors can exit on a takeover.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fourth strength is the equity value beneath the debt. At the September average repurchase price of USD 54.93 the 33.1 million shares outstanding were worth about USD 1,818.3 million, 2.08x debt principal, an analyst illustration that depends on the share price holding.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 81; calculation CALC-63; calculation CALC-64

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first weakness is shrinking, cancellable advertising revenue. Advertising was 63.09% of nine-month revenue and fell 6.30% on agreements that most often run one year or less, and retention fell below 100% in all three advertising segments, so advertisers can cut spend faster than costs can follow, which lowers the earnings that support the 2028 and 2030 notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 54–55; 10-K_2025-12-31_zd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 29; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second weakness is margin loss. EBITDA before goodwill impairment fell 29.00% for nine months and its margin to 17.35% from 23.59%, because the cost base, meaning operating costs before depreciation, amortization and goodwill impairment, rose 4.39% while revenue fell 3.48%, so operating leverage is working against creditors.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation CALC-26; calculation CALC-27; calculation CALC-28; calculation CALC-29; calculation CALC-30; calculation CALC-37

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third weakness is the use of cash. Repurchases of USD 265.0 million came while combined free cash flow was an outflow of USD 49.3 million, and at the third-quarter rate cash would last 7.09 quarters, so the cushion that protects creditors is being converted into shareholder returns without a stated floor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation CALC-10; calculation CALC-19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fourth weakness is goodwill at risk. USD 872.8 million of goodwill, 69.21% of the balance, sits in reporting units with no excess fair value or less than 15% excess, so another forecast cut would add a non-cash charge and could lower covenant earnings if impairments are not added back.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 57; calculation CALC-65; calculation CALC-66

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fifth weakness is the thin backstop and the open leverage definition. The revolving facility expires seven months after the as-of date with no extension disclosed, the covenant definitions are not supplied, and debt principal is at least 3.64x the only earnings bound the filings allow, so a weaker 2027 could meet a refinancing and a covenant test together.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ziff Davis, Inc. is a Delaware company listed on Nasdaq and run from New York. Since it sold Connectivity on June 17, 2026 it reports four segments, Technology & Shopping, Gaming & Entertainment, Health & Wellness and Cybersecurity & Martech, with nine-month revenue of USD 843.7 million that was 63.09% advertising and performance marketing, 34.97% subscription and licensing and 1.94% other. The credit link is that cash flow visibility is low for the advertising majority, which sits on short, cancellable agreements and on search and social traffic, and moderate for the subscription third, which supports debt service but is not growing: subscription revenue fell 0.38% in nine months while customer counts fell in all three segments that report them. The sale removed the segment that earned 29.68% of FY2025 segment operating income from 15.90% of revenue, so the remaining group is more exposed to advertising than the group that issued the notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 53; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-77; calculation CALC-78

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No controlling shareholder or sponsor is stated, and holders above the cover-page threshold are excluded from the non-affiliate value without being named, so no holder is shown to control the company; the proxy statement that would name directors and larger holders is not supplied. The debt sits at the parent: the 2030 senior notes are guaranteed on an unsecured basis by certain domestic wholly-owned subsidiaries whose names are not printed, the 2028 convertible notes carry no stated subsidiary guarantee and are structurally junior to all subsidiary liabilities, and the revolving facility is secured by a lien on the majority of the assets of the company and its guarantors. For creditors this means noteholders depend on cash and on guarantor value that cannot be sized from the filings, and that the secured revolver would rank first if drawn. The financial statements are consolidated for Ziff Davis, Inc. and its subsidiaries, and no parent-only or guarantor-only figures are supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The advertising majority of revenue is not predictable beyond one year. Advertising agreements run one year or less and can be ended without penalty, the company discloses no advertiser or customer concentration, and visitors arrive through search, email and social referrals while the company says search rankings fluctuate and traffic cannot be assured, so that revenue is cyclical, discretionary and exposed to substitution rather than recurring. Advertising and performance marketing fell USD 35.8 million for nine months, led by USD 22.8 million in Technology & Shopping, USD 10.0 million in Health & Wellness and USD 3.0 million in Gaming & Entertainment, and retention fell in each. The credit implication is that the 63.09% of revenue that supports most of the EBITDA has little contractual protection in a downturn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Pricing power is weak in advertising and mixed in subscriptions. Quarterly revenue per advertising customer fell to USD 109,111 from USD 132,849 in Technology & Shopping and to USD 57,224 from USD 74,053 in Gaming & Entertainment while customer counts rose, which means advertisers are spending less each, and it rose only in Health & Wellness, where customers fell to 723 from 825. In subscriptions, revenue per customer rose in Gaming & Entertainment and Health & Wellness and fell in Cybersecurity & Martech, while customers fell in all three, so price and mix are offsetting volume losses only in part; Health & Wellness customers fell 22.19%. A rising price per remaining customer cannot offset a shrinking base for long.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Seasonality favors the fourth quarter for digital media, and the third-quarter decline of 5.61% was steeper than the 2.33% of the first half, so the deceleration is not a seasonal artifact.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_zd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation CALC-22; calculation CALC-23

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Costs did not flex with revenue. Sales and marketing was 43.1% of revenue against 41.4% and direct costs 15.8% against 14.3%, and the cost base of USD 697.3 million, operating costs before depreciation, amortization and goodwill impairment, was 4.39% higher than a year earlier while revenue fell 3.48%. Employee costs, the largest line in the segment expense tables, were flat at USD 273.0 million against USD 272.7 million and partner payments rose to USD 77.6 million from USD 74.9 million, so the main cost lines did not fall with revenue. Sales and marketing of USD 363.6 million is the main lever, but it consists primarily of internet-based advertising, so cutting it could lower traffic and revenue further. The credit implication is that margins cannot be defended at current revenue without a deliberate cost program, which the filings do not describe; no restructuring cost or program is stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 46; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 60–61; calculation CALC-35; calculation CALC-36; calculation CALC-37

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Segment results show where margin is lost. Technology & Shopping lost USD 48.6 million at the operating line and Health & Wellness lost USD 16.4 million after goodwill impairments, while Gaming & Entertainment earned USD 28.0 million and Cybersecurity & Martech USD 31.2 million. Before goodwill impairment the four segments earned USD 78.6 million against USD 113.4 million, down 30.71%, with unallocated corporate cost up 23.89%. Depreciation and amortization fell as acquired intangibles run off, which flatters operating income but not EBITDA. Advertising and marketing related spending rose in Technology & Shopping and Health & Wellness, the two segments that lost revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 46; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 63; calculation CALC-41; calculation CALC-42; calculation CALC-43; calculation CALC-44

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is moderate but rising as revenue falls. Continuing capital expenditure was 9.09% of revenue for nine months against 7.52%, and total purchases of property and equipment were USD 91.1 million on the combined basis. The filings do not split maintenance from growth capital expenditure or describe what it buys, so flexibility is judged moderate: spending is spread across all four segments and rose while revenue fell, which shows it has not been cut but also that no commitment forces it. Working capital added cash through lower receivables and consumed it through lower payables, largely the gift-card float discussed below.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 48; calculation CALC-45; calculation CALC-46; calculation CALC-90

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Conversion of EBITDA to free cash flow has broken down on the combined basis. Free cash flow was 69.91% of EBITDA in FY2025 with Connectivity included and an outflow of USD 49.3 million for nine months of 2026 against an inflow of USD 130.1 million a year earlier. Cash interest was low at USD 21.5 million for nine months, leases are small, and no separate restructuring cost is stated; the company attributes the fall in operating cash flow mainly to the absence of Connectivity results and to higher income tax payments and legal and advisory fees driven by the sale, and separately reports the negative effect of the gift-card business. How much of the outflow is one-off cannot be split because discontinued operating cash flow is not printed. The credit implication is that EBITDA does not yet translate into free cash flow available for deleveraging.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 75; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-19; calculation CALC-20; calculation CALC-47; calculation CALC-91

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is intense and works on the revenue line. The company names diversified rivals such as IAC, Future PLC and Red Ventures, vertical specialists such as RVO Health, TechTarget and Vox Media, and large ad sellers such as Alphabet, Meta and Snap, some with greater resources. Falling retention in all three advertising segments is consistent with rivals and platforms taking budget, which lowers revenue and margin and the earnings that support refinancing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The threat of new entrants is moderate on the evidence in the filings. The company says its markets are highly competitive and that rivals may have cheaper pricing or more effective marketing, and generative AI makes content easier to copy and reproduce, while established brands, audience reach and exclusive advertising representation for the properties of two medical centers slow entry. The effect on creditors is gradual traffic and pricing pressure rather than a sudden break, which is an analyst reading.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The threat of substitutes is the most credit-relevant force. The company states that generative AI may reduce its online traffic and audience sizes, and it has sued OpenAI for copying its content, with no recovery or loss amount stated. Lower traffic cuts advertising and affiliate commission revenue directly, with no contractual protection, so substitution would lower the earnings that support the notes before any cost response.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Buyer power is high in advertising and moderate in subscriptions. Advertisers can cancel without penalty and retention is falling, while subscribers are consumers and small businesses paying small monthly amounts, so they can leave but no single one matters; no concentration is disclosed. The implication is that pricing cannot be raised to cover cost increases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Supplier power is high for traffic. Search engines, social platforms and ad exchanges control whether the company's pages are found and monetized, the company says search rankings fluctuate and algorithm changes can lower placement, and it has sued Google and Alphabet alleging antitrust violations related to publisher ad servers and ad exchanges. Partner payments and cloud costs add smaller supplier exposure, so a change by a platform can reduce revenue without any change in the company's own conduct.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Technology and regulation are material to credit; macroeconomic and political factors matter through advertising budgets. Generative AI may reduce referral traffic, and the law on its use of copyrighted material is unsettled, which could cut revenue or, if the company's lawsuits succeed, add recoveries that the filings do not size. Privacy class actions against Mashable and IGN under California and federal privacy statutes carry no estimable loss and none is accrued, so an adverse ruling would be an unreserved call on cash. Advertising budgets are cyclical and discretionary, and the company notes that trade and tariff policy can cause cancellations. Interest rates are higher than when the notes were issued, and the company says it may not be able to refinance fixed-rate debt at similar rates.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths that support the credit are cash above debt, a simple fixed-rate unsecured structure, no sponsor or dividend, and a subscription third of revenue; each is set out with its mechanism above. Weaknesses that constrain it are shrinking cancellable advertising revenue, falling margin, the use of cash for repurchases, goodwill at risk and a revolver that expires within a year.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-1; calculation CALC-26; calculation CALC-65

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Opportunities that could improve credit quality are limited to management's choices: repaying or repurchasing the 2030 senior notes, which traded at 91.25% of principal, with cash; extending the revolver while earnings can still support it; and recoveries from the lawsuits against OpenAI and Google, which are unquantified. Threats that could weaken it are further traffic loss to generative AI and search changes, acquisitions funded from sale cash, privacy litigation and a failure to extend the revolver.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_zd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 80; calculation CALC-60

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The financial profile is stronger on liquidity and access to capital than on earnings, and the trend is down. Liquidity position is Strong: cash of USD 1,407.7 million and USD 348.9 million of revolver availability against debt principal of USD 872.3 million, with only USD 1.1 million of implied letters of credit and USD 158.6 million of the cash, 11.26%, held abroad. Ability to refinance or access capital markets is Average: after the 1.75% repayment nothing drawn matures before March 2028 and the revolver is secured and undrawn, but the revolver expires seven months after the as-of date and the 2030 senior notes carried a disclosed fair value of 91.25% of principal. Scale and market position is Average: nine-month revenue of USD 843.7 million is down 3.48%, and management cites reach of more than 440 million monthly users for IGN, but advertisers are spending less each.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 73; 10-K_2025-12-31_zd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation CALC-3; calculation CALC-60; calculation CALC-73

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competitive advantage, business diversification, and cost and capex flexibility are Average. Four segments and two revenue types spread the risk, no customer concentration is disclosed and the United States supplies most revenue, but the advertising majority behaves as one exposure to search and social traffic, and cost lines rose while revenue fell. Financial policy and governance is Average: no sponsor, no dividend, effective internal control and change-of-control protection for creditors are offset by repurchases that exceeded free cash flow in FY2024 and by the absence of any cash floor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-K_2025-12-31_zd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-K_2025-12-31_zd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-K_2025-12-31_zd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 196; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-78; calculation CALC-81; calculation CALC-82

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margin stability and free cash flow stability are Weak. EBITDA before goodwill impairment margin fell to 17.35% from 23.59%, the third quarter margin was 14.39% against 25.84%, and combined free cash flow swung from an inflow of USD 130.1 million to an outflow of USD 49.3 million. Trend is down on revenue, margin and cash flow; the key missing datapoints are recast continuing-basis annual results, covenant definitions and compliance ratios, the use of the remaining sale cash and management guidance.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-19; calculation CALC-20; calculation CALC-29; calculation CALC-30; calculation CALC-33; calculation CALC-34

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Debt is shown below as the notes and credit agreement print it, with the maturity wall by year; principal and carrying value reconcile through unamortized discount and issuance costs.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Claims outside the debt figure are listed with whether the filings count them in debt; none is added to debt or netted against cash in this synthesis.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The primary downside path is a further loss of search and AI referral traffic that cuts cancellable advertising revenue while costs hold, which lowers EBITDA below the interest and covenant needs just as the revolver comes up for renewal and cash has been spent on repurchases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_zd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-K_2025-12-31_zd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; calculation CALC-6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 months to 24 months the outlook is stable for liquidity and negative for earnings. Tailwinds are the cash balance, the removal of the 1.75% maturity, and interest income on cash that already exceeded interest expense in the third quarter. Headwinds are falling advertising retention, generative AI and search changes cutting traffic, the revolver expiry in June 2027, the 2028 convertible notes that holders can convert freely from December 2027, tax and fees on the sale gain, and a repurchase authorization that runs to 2036. Whether earnings recover depends on the fourth quarter, which in 2025 earned 34.97% of total-entity EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next three to five years the credit turns on whether the continuing portfolio stabilizes below its current size and whether the cash is applied to the 2028 and 2030 notes or to shareholders and acquisitions. The company has deployed about USD 3.3 billion on acquisitions since 2012 and calls programmatic acquisition a tenet of its strategy, so a return to acquisitions funded from sale cash is the main medium-term headwind, while a smaller note stack of USD 723.2 million is a tailwind if cash repays it. No company guidance is supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The downside begins with a further loss of search and AI referral traffic, the risk the company names for its audience and the pressure it cites for the Technology & Shopping decline, together with advertiser budget cuts that the one-year, cancellable agreements allow. The first operating break is in Technology & Shopping and Health & Wellness, where the reporting units with no excess fair value sit: advertising revenue falls faster than the 6.30% of nine months while the cost base, which rose 4.39%, stays near current levels, so EBITDA before goodwill impairment falls below the USD 41.6 million of the third quarter. The financial transmission is further non-cash impairments from the USD 872.8 million of goodwill with little or no headroom, lower covenant earnings if impairments are not added back, and free cash flow that stays negative as in the third quarter, when the combined outflow after capital expenditure was USD 100.07 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 56–57; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 69; 10-K_2025-12-31_zd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 29; calculation CALC-7; calculation CALC-5; calculation CALC-31; calculation CALC-37; calculation CALC-65; calculation CALC-92

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The liquidity consequence arrives through cash: at the third-quarter rate of fall of USD 198.4 million cash would last 7.09 quarters before the USD 279.95 million of near claims, so continued repurchases with a negative operating cash flow would leave the 2028 convertible notes of USD 263.1 million to be met from a much smaller cash balance, an illustration and not a forecast. The leverage and refinancing consequence is that the revolver would need to be extended in mid-2027 on a covenant package tested against lower earnings, and debt principal is already at least 3.64x the only earnings bound available. Management has several levers: it can stop repurchases, which were USD 92.0 million in the third quarter, cut sales and marketing of USD 363.6 million, defer capital expenditure, repay or repurchase notes below par, or sell further businesses. Resilience is sufficient to avoid liquidity distress within 24 months because those levers are within management's control and cash is large; it is not sufficient if repurchases and acquisitions continue while earnings fall. Observable triggers are advertising retention below 85%, quarterly EBITDA before goodwill impairment below USD 41.6 million, cash below USD 1,000 million, no revolver extension by March 2027, and repurchases above USD 92.0 million in a quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 61; calculation CALC-4; calculation CALC-6; calculation CALC-10; calculation CALC-14; calculation CALC-54

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Ziff Davis presents an adequate business profile supported by cash of USD 535.4 million above debt principal, with pro forma cash after the 1.75% repayment not established, an undrawn revolver, fixed-rate unsecured debt with no drawn maturity before March 2028 after that repayment, and no sponsor or dividend, but credit quality is constrained by shrinking, cancellable advertising revenue, a margin that fell to 17.35% from 23.59% before goodwill impairment, USD 872.8 million of goodwill with little or no headroom and a policy of returning cash to shareholders. Cash-flow durability appears weak because free cash flow was an outflow of USD 49.3 million for nine months on the combined basis and 69.91% of EBITDA converted to free cash flow only in FY2025 with Connectivity included. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on extending the revolver before its June 2027 expiry, on earnings recovering in the fourth quarter, and on how much of the sale cash remains by March 2028. The primary downside path is traffic and advertiser losses that lower earnings while cash is spent. A comparison with typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector is not established because no peer set is supplied. Further analysis would require recast continuing-basis annual results, the executed credit agreement and covenant definitions, the date and effect of the 1.75% repayment and tax payment, and management guidance. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: shareholder returns and falling advertising earnings eroding the sale cash before the 2028 convertible notes and the revolver renewal.

fields.value: The column headed As written holds each figure as the findings state it. EBITDA is derived as operating income plus depreciation and amortization, because the company states none.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The orchestrator selects the next module.
